title: Ingress-side probabilistic de-duplication (bloom filter credit-guard) for at-least-once billing safety
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add an ingress-side probabilistic de-duplication layer to reduce duplicate consumption accounting from at-least-once delivery semantics. The solution uses a time-partitioned Bloom filter at the edge proxy to short-circuit obvious retries, combined with a backend reconciliation pass that applies precise ledger corrections for false positives/negatives. Goal: eliminate >99.9% billing duplicates for transient retries without requiring synchronous global coordination on the hot path.
acceptance_criteria: 0.999+ reduction in duplicate billable units from simulated 2x-5x retry storms in staging
No more than 0.05% increase in 95th percentile ingress latency at p50/p95 compared to baseline
Automated reconciliation job produces zero net revenue loss > 0.1% over 7-day runs and provides per-customer audit rows
End-to-end e2e integration tests that inject duplicate sequences and assert single-billing rows
Design and implementation reviewed and approved by Security and Billing teams
design_notes: Ingress component keeps a per-region, time-windowed Bloom filter keyed by (customer_id, ingest_nonce_hash, request_type) with a 10-minute sliding window
Bloom filter tuned for single-producer per-customer memory budgets (configurable per plan) and uses delta-snapshots to disk for cold restarts

On a Bloom-hit, the proxy cancels forwarding to the main ingest path and responds with an idempotent receipt acknowledging prior acceptance; hits are recorded to an eventual-consistency ledger for audit

On Bloom-miss, request proceeds normally and the ingest pipeline writes canonical consumption rows; each accepted request writes an acknowledgement token back to an append-only ledger used by reconciliation

Reconciliation job cross-checks append-only ledger entries with final consumption commits to detect Bloom false positives (which hide duplicates) and produces corrective credit/debit entries per customer
Fallback: if proxy fails or Bloom filter memory exhausted, we fallback to deterministic nonce-windowing in the backend to guarantee correctness at expense of additional backend coordination latency
We will expose per-customer tuning knobs: bloom_size_bytes, window_seconds, and aggressive_mode to balance false-positive risk vs memory/latency

ENG-90023 add ingress acknowledgement API and idempotent receipt format
ENG-90024 implement reconciliation worker and corrections ledger writer

risks_and_mitigations: False positives in Bloom filter can cause missed billing; mitigate by reconciliation job that credits/detects lost rows and by conservative default Bloom sizes
Increased ingress CPU/memory; mitigate by per-plan limits and feature gates (trial customers get default conservative settings)
Operational complexity during rollout; mitigate with gradual canary per-region and realtime dashboards showing bloom-hit rates and reconciliation deltas
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal dogfood in staging with synthetic retry storms (2 weeks)
Phase 1: Canary 1% of production traffic for non-SLA customers with aggressive monitoring (1 week)
Phase 2: Expand to 20% with per-customer tuning and reconciliation enabled (2 weeks)
Phase 3: Global rollout with automatic fallback to backend nonce-windowing for customers with any negative signals
migration_plan: Backfill: run reconciliation for last 30 days for customers that opt in during first 2 weeks; for historical windows where bloom was not present, rely on existing ledger reconciliation pipeline. Provide a one-time audit CSV per-customer for transparency.
